subject: Post-demo: Hosted API trial access strategy and ratebound proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Hosted API trial access strategy and ratebound proposal

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can keep momentum on the hosted evaluation:

1) Summary of fit from demo: your main asks were low-latency chat completions for customer-facing assistants, economical token costs at ~3M tokens/month, and strict data isolation (no shared datasets) for PII flows. Hosted API looks like a viable pilot given your traffic profile; Dedicated or Private may be needed once throughput or regulatory constraints increase.

2) Proposed pilot scope (hosted):
- 2 sandbox endpoints (chat-short and chat-long) mapped to a 13B quantized variant.
- Token budget slice: ~3M tokens/mo for pilot.
- Ratebound proposal: baseline 120 RPS aggregate with burst to 250 RPS for short bursts (see detail below).
- Prefetch/KV caching: enable prefix caching for session starters likely to reduce token counts ~15-30%.

3) Ops/access: we can provision sandbox API keys + ephemeral credentials for your engineers. I'll attach a short checklist for quickstart and a feature matrix we referenced (see attachments).

4) Questions for you: can you confirm the top 5 entry points where the assistant will be used (webchat, mobile chat, email triage, support search, internal ops)? This will help the endpoint mapping and rate cap plan.

Next actions we recommend:
- Redwood: provision sandbox keys + sample endpoint mapping; provide short doc on ratebound behaviour and prefetch implications (Ben on copy).
- Acme: confirm entry points and a single point of contact for sandbox access/testing.
- Schedule: propose a 60-minute tech touch next week to walk your SRE through throttling and KV cache behavior.

Attachments: feature-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted API trial access strategy and ratebound proposal

Thanks Soojin — solid recap. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock the pilot: 

- Entry points: webchat (primary), mobile chat, transactional email summaries (low volume), support ticket auto-classify, and post-call note drafts.
- The 3M tokens/mo target is a starting point; if background batch jobs (summaries) spike we may need to route them to a different endpoint or schedule off-peak.

Questions: 
1) Ratebound: does the 120 RPS baseline mean per-endpoint or global for our account? We want predictable per-endpoint guarantees for the webchat traffic.
2) Prefetch/KV caching: is this transparent to the client SDK or do we need to change our session management?
3) Data isolation: when you say "hosted with isolation", what does that mean for logs and model telemetry in the hosted mode? Are logs accessible to other customers?

Also, can you share the sandbox access SLA (if any) and the expected time to ramp RPS if the trial looks good?

— Sam
Sam Park
Head of Product
Acme AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted API trial access strategy and ratebound proposal

Hi Sam — answers inline: 

> 1) Ratebound: does the 120 RPS baseline mean per-endpoint or global for our account?
We typically provision a global account-level baseline and allow per-endpoint shaping. For your use case we recommend reserving 80 RPS for webchat endpoint and allocating the remaining 40 RPS across mobile and background endpoints; bursts are handled at the account level up to 250 RPS for short durations. We'll reflect this in the sandbox mapping.

> 2) Prefetch/KV caching: is this transparent to the client SDK or do we need to change our session management?
Prefetch and KV caching are runtime features. For best results you should continue to send session ids with requests so the runtime can attach the KV cache appropriately — no SDK changes required, just consistent session identifiers. We will share a short snippet for session-affinity patterns in the sandbox doc.

> 3) Data isolation: when you say "hosted with isolation", what does that mean for logs and model telemetry in the hosted mode? Are logs accessible to other customers?
Hosted mode provides logical isolation: your requests and logs are stored under your tenant id and are not visible to other customers. Some anonymized telemetry (e.g., per-model performance stats) is aggregated across tenants for platform health, but we do not surface request-level logs to other customers. If you need stricter controls (no aggregates), Dedicated or Private options are available.

SLA and ramp: sandbox access is provided with best-effort support (no SLA) but we can guarantee a 24–48 hour turnaround for provisioning. For production pilot uplift to dedicated capacity we have a standard lead time of 2–4 weeks depending on capacity and region.

Sandbox link and quickstart: https://drive.google.com/hosted-quickstart-sandbox (credentials to be issued once POC contact confirmed). Also attaching the hosted quickstart checklist.

I'll prepare an endpoint mapping proposal for your webchat/mobile split and share by Monday.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
